cohort: The study included 895 female patients with locoregional nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), of whom 79 conceived after treatment, and a matched group of 315 non-pregnant patients for survival analysis.
finding: Pregnancy after nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) treatment was not associated with adverse clinical outcomes (OS, DFS, LRFS, or DMFS) for the mothers, and no abnormalities were recorded in any of the newborns.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rate among those who successfully delivered after NPC treatment was 30.1%.
birth_weight: Median birth weight of newborns was 3.11 kg
